title: How to create a Quick Step in Outlook on Mac: what to use instead
metaTitle: How to Create a Quick Step in Outlook on Mac
description: How to create a Quick Step in Outlook on Mac: Quick Steps are not in the Mac app. Here is what to use, with steps for Rules and Outlook on the web.

intro: You cannot create a Quick Step in Outlook on Mac, because the Quick steps feature is not in the Mac app. The closest working options are a rule in Outlook for Mac, or Quick steps in Outlook on the web for Exchange Online accounts.
tldr: Quick Steps is not in Outlook for Mac, based on Microsoft's pages and a 2024 community answer.
The closest Mac option is a rule: Outlook > Settings > Rules > +Add Rule.
For a button-style Quick step, open Outlook on the web with an Exchange Online account.
Legacy Outlook for Mac uses Tools > Rules, and Microsoft says its support ends in October 2026.
Check Microsoft's Outlook for Mac pages after each update before you assume Quick Steps has arrived.

blocks.title: Check your version first
blocks.text: Quick steps is missing from the Mac app, so the steps below use rules instead. Confirm which Outlook you run before you start.
Does Outlook for Mac have Quick Steps?

No. The Quick steps feature is missing from Outlook for Mac, based on the sources I checked for this page. Microsoft's own Quick steps article covers new Outlook for Windows, classic Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web. It never mentions Mac or macOS.

A second clue comes from Microsoft Community. In April 2024, a moderator marked a reply as the most helpful answer. It said Quick Step functionality is not available in Outlook for Mac. The reply gave no release date. The thread is tagged Legacy Outlook for Mac, so keep that in mind.

A third clue is a 2026 comparison from Carly, a third-party site dated April 7, 2026. It marks Quick Steps as Full in classic Outlook for Windows, Partial in new Outlook and Outlook on the web, and No in Outlook for Mac. A third-party table is not proof. It does match what Microsoft's Mac pages leave out.
I found no Microsoft announcement that Mac support is coming. That could change. So the rest of this page gives you the closest working options today, and a way to check for updates yourself.
What a Quick Step does, and why people want one

A Quick Step is a set of actions behind one button. Microsoft describes Quick steps as a way to automate common or repetitive tasks. Instead of moving a message, flagging it and replying in three separate moves, you click once.

Think about someone who files supplier invoices every morning. Each invoice needs a move to a folder and a short reply that confirms receipt. A Quick Step can hold both actions, so the morning goes faster. Small savings like that add up on a busy inbox.

The volume explains why these tools matter. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index says the average worker receives 117 emails a day, and most are skimmed in under 60 seconds. The same report says employees are interrupted every 2 minutes during core work hours.
Those numbers are about attention, not clicks. A repeat task pulls attention away every time it appears. Removing that pull matters more than the click itself.
Check the Home tab and Help menu on your Mac

Open Outlook and look at the Home tab. The sources above do not show a Quick steps group on the Mac, so do not spend long hunting for one. Then open the Help menu and search for Quick steps. If nothing relevant appears, your build does not have the feature.
Quick steps can exist in other versions while the Mac app is missing them. That is why the next sections focus on the tools the Mac app does have.
Option 1: create a rule in Outlook for Mac

A rule is the closest match on the Mac. It does not look like a button, but it files and sorts mail the same way. In the current Outlook for Mac, rules live under Settings. Microsoft says you can only create server rules in this app, because client rules are no longer supported.

Here is a worked example. Say you want all mail from your accountant in a folder called Tax 2026. Use the sender as the condition, pick the move action, and choose the folder. Test it on last month's mail before you trust it.
Use a rule when the job should happen on its own. Mail from one sender goes to a folder. A word in the subject gets flagged. Once you save it, you do not click anything.

Mail > Home > Quick steps > Manage quick steps

blocks.text: Option 2: make a quick rule from the Home tab
A quick rule is the fastest way in. Select one message first. Then go to Home > Rules. You get three choices: Move Messages from, Move Messages to, or Create Rule.
Outlook fills in the sender, recipient or subject from the message you selected. That means you rarely type anything. Check the filled-in text before you save, because a sender address can change.
Quick rules suit one sender or one recipient. When the logic has two parts, such as a sender plus a keyword, open the full rule form from Settings instead.
Option 3: use Quick steps in Outlook on the web

If you need the real Quick steps, use Outlook on the web in a browser. Safari and Chrome both work for it. Quick steps there work only for Exchange Online accounts, according to the Carly guide. POP3, IMAP and Outlook.com personal accounts are not supported.

items: Open Outlook on the web in your browser and sign in.
Select Mail, then open the Home tab.
Click Quick steps, then select Manage quick steps.
In the Settings window, under Quick steps, select +New quick step.
Enter a Name for the quick step.
Under Choose an action, pick an action.
Select Save, or keep customizing to add more detail.

blocks.text: To change a quick step later, return to Manage quick steps and use the Edit quick step icon. Keep names short so you can spot them quickly.
Limits and edge cases in the browser
Quick steps in Outlook on the web do not run against shared mailboxes, according to the Carly guide. Check how the mailbox is set up before you build a step for it.

Quick steps also cannot be undone with a menu command or a keyboard shortcut such as Ctrl+Z. Some actions, such as Permanently Delete, cannot be reversed at all. Test a new quick step on one message first.
A step that moves mail out of the inbox can make a message look lost. Search the folder list before you panic. The message is usually in the folder the step chose.
If you still use legacy Outlook for Mac

Microsoft's Outlook for Mac page says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026. That month has already passed, so confirm which app you run before you change anything. You can try the new app by turning off the Legacy Outlook switch.
To go back, choose Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook. Accounts added in one version are not added to the other automatically, so add them again in the app you use.

items: Under Client Rules (IMAP/POP) or Exchange Servers, select the account.
Click Add, name the rule, then set its conditions and actions.

blocks.text: The legacy app has no Quick steps either. Use the rule path instead, which the legacy app supports through its own Tools menu.
Mistakes people make when they switch from Windows

items: Hunting for a Quick steps group on the Home tab. The Mac app does not show one in the sources checked, so go straight to Settings > Rules.
Building a quick step in the browser, then expecting it in the Mac app. Each version keeps its own setup.
Skipping the test. Run a new rule on a few existing messages first, so you can see what it catches.
Forgetting the account type. Personal and IMAP accounts do not get web Quick steps.
Expecting Ctrl+Shift shortcuts to work on a Mac. Microsoft lists those keys for the Windows and web versions, and no source checked maps them to Command.

blocks.text: A rule that files mail is easy to undo. Turn it off with the toggle, and mail already moved stays where it went. Fix the rule, then run it again on a test batch.
Check for updates before you assume the answer has changed

Microsoft's Outlook for Mac page lists 16.42 (20101102) as the minimum Current Channel build. Newer builds are the place to look first. A 2024 moderator suggested watching the Outlook Blog for announcements, so check that blog after big updates.
If Quick steps reaches a future Mac build, follow Microsoft's steps for that version, not the steps on this page. Rules will still work the same way.
What to do next

If the rule worked, read [how to create a rule in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook) for more conditions and exceptions. To give that rule a home, [create a folder in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-folder-in-outlook) first. If your inbox splits mail in two, [turning off Focused Inbox](/how-to/turn-off-focused-inbox-in-outlook) changes what you see.
For help with the Outlook screens themselves, see [the Outlook on Mac assistant page](/apps/outlook). Lazur points at buttons and explains each field. It does not click for you.

faq.question: Can I create a Quick Step in Outlook on Mac?
faq.answer: Not in the Outlook for Mac app, based on Microsoft's Quick steps article and a 2024 Microsoft Community answer. Use a rule in the Mac app, or create Quick steps in Outlook on the web if your account is Exchange Online.

faq.question: Is a rule the same thing as a Quick Step?
faq.answer: No. A Quick Step is a button that runs a set of actions when you click it. A rule runs when mail arrives and matches its conditions, so you do not need to click anything.

faq.question: Why does Outlook on the web have Quick steps when the Mac app does not?
faq.answer: Microsoft documents Quick steps for Outlook on the web and for both Outlook versions on Windows. Its article never mentions Mac or macOS. For Mac users, the browser is the route to Quick steps in the sources checked.

faq.question: Will Quick Steps come to Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft has not announced it in the sources checked for this page. A 2024 moderator gave no date and suggested the Outlook Blog. Check that blog before you assume either way.

faq.question: Does legacy Outlook for Mac have Quick Steps?
faq.answer: No source I checked lists Quick steps for legacy Outlook for Mac. Its rules sit under Tools > Rules. Microsoft says legacy support ends in October 2026, a month that has already passed.

faq.question: What is the Quick Step keyboard shortcut on a Mac?
faq.answer: The sources checked do not give one. Microsoft lists Ctrl+Shift 5 through 9 for Quick steps in New Outlook and the web, but does not say how those keys map to Command on a Mac keyboard.

faq.question: Can I use Quick steps on a shared mailbox?
faq.answer: Not according to the Carly guide, which says Quick steps do not run against shared mailboxes. Check with your administrator about how rules work on that mailbox.

faq.question: Where does Lazur fit in?
faq.answer: Lazur points at the Rules page and the +Add Rule button, and explains each field as you go. It does not click those buttons for you.

steps.name: Open Outlook settings
steps.text: Click Outlook in the menu bar, then select Settings. The Settings window opens with a list of options.
steps.tip: If Settings does not appear, make sure Outlook is the active app first.

steps.name: Open the Rules page
steps.text: In the Settings window, select Rules. Any rules you already have appear in a list.

steps.name: Start a new rule
steps.text: Click +Add Rule. A new rule form opens with an empty name and empty conditions.

steps.name: Name the rule
steps.text: Type a name you will recognize later, such as Supplier invoices to Finance. Clear names help when you have many rules.

steps.name: Choose a condition
steps.text: Under Select a Condition, pick what the rule checks, such as the sender, a word in the subject, or the recipient.

steps.name: Choose an action
steps.text: Under Select an action, pick what should happen. To file mail, choose the action that moves the message, then pick the folder.

steps.name: Add extra conditions or exceptions
steps.text: Optional. Add a second condition to narrow the rule, or an exception so the rule skips certain mail.

steps.name: Decide whether to stop other rules
steps.text: Choose whether to Stop processing more rules. Turn it on when this rule should be the last one that applies to a message.

steps.name: Save the rule
steps.text: Click Save. The rule appears in your list, ready to test or edit.

steps.name: Test, edit, or turn off
steps.text: Use the three-dot menu next to the rule to edit it or run it now. Use the toggle to turn it off, and reorder rules when the order matters.
steps.tip: Run the rule on a few existing messages first, so you can see what it catches.

troubleshooting.problem: No Quick steps option in the Mac app
troubleshooting.fix: That matches the sources. Use Settings > Rules for a rule, or open Outlook on the web for Quick steps.

troubleshooting.problem: Rule created but mail is not moving
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the rule's toggle is on and that the condition matches the message. Use the three-dot menu to run the rule now on a test message.

troubleshooting.problem: Web Quick steps missing for my account
troubleshooting.fix: Quick steps in Outlook on the web need an Exchange Online account. POP3, IMAP and Outlook.com personal accounts do not qualify.

troubleshooting.problem: Legacy Outlook shows no Rules page in Settings
troubleshooting.fix: You are probably in legacy Outlook. Use Tools > Rules and choose the account under Client Rules or Exchange Servers.

troubleshooting.problem: Not sure which Outlook you run
troubleshooting.fix: Open Help. If you see Revert to Legacy Outlook, you are in the new app.

troubleshooting.problem: An account is missing in one version
troubleshooting.fix: Accounts added in one version are not added to the other. Add the account again in the version you use.
